parties: Plaintiff: Kingsley Shih and Andrew Wang Fat Wong
Defendant: Wah Ying Cheong Company Limited

facts.F1: The applicants, Kingsley Shih and Andrew Wang Fat Wong, are the tenants of adjacent ground floor flats in the premises known as "Vista do Vale" situated at Numbers 2 and 4 Sha Tin Heights Road, Sha Tin in the New Territories.
facts.F2: The subject premises are located immediately above the Tai Po Road where it overlooks the Sha Tin New Town.
facts.F3: The two-storey premises comprising four flats were erected in 1956, and over the intervening years, have fallen into a state of dilapidation.
facts.F4: The applicants' flats are both habitable but have suffered from the landlord's reluctance to carry out regular maintenance.
facts.F5: The landlord has applied for a modification of the crown lease conditions to allow for redevelopment of the property.
facts.F6: The landlord has estimated that redevelopment will commence in about a year's time, but this timeline is considered too vague.
facts.F7: The applicants sought new tenancies for 2 and 3 years, respectively, from 1st January 1988.
facts.F8: The Tribunal considered the comparable lettings of nearby properties, including The Pink House and Chase Villa, but noted that they are superior in condition and amenities to the subject premises.
facts.F9: The Tribunal noted the larger but unfenced garden of the subject premises, lack of mains water supply, and other differences in condition and amenities.
facts.F10: The Tribunal applied a unit rate of $3.30 per sq. ft. to the subject premises.

facts.F1: The Premises were let to the Defendant for a period of three years from 11 October 1999 to 10 October 2002 under a lease dated 11 October 1999.
facts.F2: The Defendant defaulted in the payment of rent and other charges.
facts.F3: The Plaintiff commenced proceedings in the District Court on 19 January 2001, which were transferred to the High Court on 4 September 2001 (HCA 4145/2001).
facts.F4: The Plaintiff claimed damages for repudiation based on the acceptance of the Defendant's repudiation of the Lease.
facts.F5: Damages were claimed under four heads: rental loss from 1 February 2001 to 25 September 2002, service charges from 1 February 2001 to 25 September 2002, office rates from 1 April 2001 to 25 September 2002, and legal costs from 15 January 2001 to 19 September 2002.
facts.F6: The Defendant disputes both liability and quantum, alleging the existence of an oral collateral contract and that the Plaintiff has not mitigated its loss.
facts.F7: The Premises were left unoccupied subsequent to the termination of the Lease and remained unoccupied until 25 September 2002.
facts.F8: The court found that the Defendant repudiated the Lease.
facts.F9: The court held that the Plaintiff had accepted such repudiation.
facts.F10: The Plaintiff's attempts to let the Premises following the termination of the Lease were deemed reasonable by the court.
facts.F11: The Defendant's evidence on mitigation of loss was deemed insufficient by the court.
facts.F12: A Master will assess the balance of damages due to the Plaintiff.

facts.F4: The company was found to be a quasi-partnership in previous proceedings (HCCW 282/2010) and the 1st respondent was found to have conducted the affairs of the company in a way that was unfairly prejudicial to the petitioner.

facts.F7: The 1st respondent did not comply with the buyout order, and instead caused the company to enter into a transaction with Heathcliff Trading SA, which resulted in a deficit of HK$495 million on the company's balance sheet.
facts.F8: All the assets of the company have been charged to Heathcliff under a debenture that creates both a fixed charge and a floating charge.
facts.F9: The 1st respondent caused the company to be put into liquidation under section 228A of the Companies (Winding-Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap 32) on 3 November 2014.
facts.F10: The petitioner applied for a permanent stay of the voluntary winding up, which was granted by Anthony Chan J on 12 January 2015.
facts.F11: The petitioner applied for the appointment of provisional liquidators in respect of the company on 18 December 2014.
